Name: Ms. Justice Gita Mittal
Biodata: Justice Gita Mittal was born on 9th December, 1958 to parents who were in academics. An alumna of the Lady Irwin Higher Secondary School [Science batch of 1975], Lady Shri Ram College For Women [BA (Eco. Hons.) 1978] and the Campus Law Centre, Delhi University [(LL.B) 1981], she was appointed as an Additional Judge of Delhi High Court on 16th July, 2004. Prior to her appointment as Additional Judge, she had an illustrious legal practice in all courts and other judicial forums since 1981. Justice Mittal was confirmed as a permanent judge on the 20th of February, 2006. As a judge, she has presided over several jurisdictions including heading a Division Bench hearing criminal appeals involving life and death sentence references; matters of the Armed Forces; Cooperative Societies; Criminal Contempt References; Criminal Appeals; Death References; Company Appeals; Writ Petitions and Letters Patent Appeals relating to the Armed Forces. She currently presides over a Division Bench hearing writ petitions arising out of orders of the Central Administrative Tribunal and other service matters. Since August, 2008, Justice Gita Mittal has been a member of the Governing Council of the National Law University, Delhi. She is also a member of the Governing Council of the Indian Law Institute, New Delhi since 2013 and has been nominated to its Administrative Committee. Justice Mittal is presently chairing the court committees on the Delhi High Court's Mediation and Conciliation Centre as well as the committee monitoring the Implementation of Judicial Guidelines for Dealing with Cases of Sexual Offences and Child Witnesses. She has spearheaded the Vulnerable Witness Court Project in the trial courts in Delhi leading to the first such court room in India being inaugurated on 16th September, 2012 and the second on 11th September, 2013. She has also served on the COFEPOSA Advisory Board, under the Conservation of Foreign Exchange & Prevention of Smuggling Act, 1974; and the committee responsible for assessing the performance of judicial officers for their recommendation for elevation as Judge of the Delhi High Court. She was appointed as a single judge Tribunal under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act, 1967 in February, 2008 to examine the Government ban on activities of the Students of Islamic Movement in India SIMI. Deeply engaged with the work of institutional strengthening, Justice Mittal has also served as a member of the Committee Against Sexual Harassment of Women at Work Place; Working Conditions and Welfare Committee For Judicial Officers/staff of High Court and District Courts; Committee to assess the performance of additional Judges of this Court while recommending their appointment as permanent Judges and to assess the judgments of additional Judges for the purpose of extension of their terms as additional Judges; Library Committee; Committee on Introduction of Evening Courts/Shift System in Subordinate Courts; and the Examination-cum-Judicial Education and Training Programme Committee. She has been engaged in conducting programmes on several topics of social relevance including gender and disability sensitisation; environment; disaster management and constitutional rights of the marginalised. Justice Mittal has been invited to contribute to national and international discussions at various forums and to present papers on topics including those relating to access to justice for the disadvantaged; gender issues; protection of human rights; impact of incarceration on women; corporate social responsibility; death penalty; impact of religion, culture, tradition on judging; corporate laws; procedure and intellectual property litigation and environmental laws and issues. Her judicial pronouncements include judgements on compensation for riot victims; right to shelter of internally displaced persons; right to marriage of a lady member of the Armed Force; the appointment of a person suffering from ‘Disorder of Sexual Differentiation’ into the para-military force; principles which would govern DNA testing in paternity issues in the absence of statutory provisions; the conducting of trials in cases involving sexual offences and recording of statements of the victims and guidelines for the same; governance of sports and sports bodies; issues involving termination of service because of a pregnancy; right to workers in the labour force; trade-mark litigation; privacy laws; contours of the right to privacy of a public figure; revocation of passport – when permissible; constitutionality of enhancement of court fee; public interest, communication and commercial disputes of a wide nature. Prior to her elevation, she was a member of the Delhi University Court from 3rd April, 1999 to 2nd April, 2004. She was nominated to the Governing Body of Ram Lal Anand College serving its member from 12th November, 1997 to 11th November, 1999. While in school, she was awarded the President's Guide Certificate by the President of India in 1974. She has represented India & Bharat Scouts and Guides at an International Global Ecology Event (Earth 'n' Us) in the USA in 1974 and studied global ecology and its preservation, in the area of air, energy, ocean, land and human resources. In 1978, she was again invited and participated as a unit leader in an international performing arts event Melody 'n' Makebelieve in the USA and thereafter in 1979 in other capacities. She has represented Delhi at the National level open championships and also captained Delhi Juniors in volleyball. She was the Sports President of the Lady Shri Ram College (1977-1978) and was the recipient of All Round Best Sports Person Award of the College in 1978. She received the Distinguished Alumna Award in 2008 from the Vice President of India, awarded by the Lady Shriram College for Women. The citation for the award reads that she is being recognized “for her landmark judgements which have ensured long-denied justice for the victimized; for the courage of her convictions and her indomitable spirit in turning challenges into opportunities; for her visionary tenacity in striving to uphold the basic right to human dignity.” Appointed as Chief Justice of High Court of Jammu & Kashmir vide Notification No. K.13021/1/2018-US.II dated 3rd August,2018 and took oath of office on 11th August,2018.

She has spearheaded the Vulnerable Witness Court Project in the trial courts in Delhi leading to the first such court room in India being inaugurated on 16th September, 2012 and the second on 11th September, 2013. She has also served on the COFEPOSA Advisory Board, under the Conservation of Foreign Exchange & Prevention of Smuggling Act, 1974; and the committee responsible for assessing the performance of judicial officers for their recommendation for elevation as Judge of the Delhi High Court. She was appointed as a single judge Tribunal under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act, 1967 in February, 2008 to examine the Government ban on activities of the Students of Islamic Movement in India SIMI. Deeply engaged with the work of institutional strengthening, Justice Mittal has also served as a member of the Committee Against Sexual Harassment of Women at Work Place; Working Conditions and Welfare Committee For Judicial Officers/staff of High Court and District Courts; Committee to assess the performance of additional Judges of this Court while recommending their appointment as permanent Judges and to assess the judgments of additional Judges for the purpose of extension of their terms as additional Judges; Library Committee; Committee on Introduction of Evening Courts/Shift System in Subordinate Courts; and the Examination-cum-Judicial Education and Training Programme Committee. She has been engaged in conducting programmes on several topics of social relevance including gender and disability sensitisation; environment; disaster management and constitutional rights of the marginalised. Justice Mittal has been invited to contribute to national and international discussions at various forums and to present papers on topics including those relating to access to justice for the disadvantaged; gender issues; protection of human rights; impact of incarceration on women; corporate social responsibility; death penalty; impact of religion, culture, tradition on judging; corporate laws; procedure and intellectual property litigation and environmental laws and issues. Her judicial pronouncements include judgements on compensation for riot victims; right to shelter of internally displaced persons; right to marriage of a lady member of the Armed Force; the appointment of a person suffering from ‘Disorder of Sexual Differentiation’ into the para-military force; principles which would govern DNA testing in paternity issues in the absence of statutory provisions; the conducting of trials in cases involving sexual offences and recording of statements of the victims and guidelines for the same; governance of sports and sports bodies; issues involving termination of service because of a pregnancy; right to workers in the labour force; trade-mark litigation; privacy laws; contours of the right to privacy of a public figure; revocation of passport – when permissible; constitutionality of enhancement of court fee; public interest, communication and commercial disputes of a wide nature. Prior to her elevation, she was a member of the Delhi University Court from 3rd April, 1999 to 2nd April, 2004. She was nominated to the Governing Body of Ram Lal Anand College serving its member from 12th November, 1997 to 11th November, 1999. While in school, she was awarded the President's Guide Certificate by the President of India in 1974. She has represented India & Bharat Scouts and Guides at an International Global Ecology Event (Earth 'n' Us) in the USA in 1974 and studied global ecology and its preservation, in the area of air, energy, ocean, land and human resources. In 1978, she was again invited and participated as a unit leader in an international performing arts event Melody 'n' Makebelieve in the USA and thereafter in 1979 in other capacities. She has represented Delhi at the National level open championships and also captained Delhi Juniors in volleyball. She was the Sports President of the Lady Shri Ram College (1977-1978) and was the recipient of All Round Best Sports Person Award of the College in 1978. She received the Distinguished Alumna Award in 2008 from the Vice President of India, awarded by the Lady Shriram College for Women. The citation for the award reads that she is being recognized “for her landmark judgements which have ensured long-denied justice for the victimized; for the courage of her convictions and her indomitable spirit in turning challenges into opportunities; for her visionary tenacity in striving to uphold the basic right to human dignity.” Appointed as Chief Justice of High Court of Jammu & Kashmir vide Notification No. K.13021/1/2018-US.II dated 3rd August,2018 and took oath of office on 11th August,2018.

Name: Ms. Justice Indira Banerjee
Biodata: Born on 24th September, 1957. Passed Indian School Certificate Examination from Loreto House, Calcutta. Graduated with History (Hons.) from Presidency College, then affiliated to Calcutta University. LL.B from Calcutta University, College of Law. Enrolled as an Advocate on 5th July, 1985. Practiced both in the Original and Appellate Sides of the Calcutta High Court in all branches of law except Criminal law, with appearances in the Supreme Court, other Courts and Tribunals. Elevated as a permanent Judge of Calcutta High Court on 5-2-2002. Chairperson of the Calcutta High Court Services Committee for almost 4 years. Officiated as Executive Chairperson of West Bengal State Legal Services Authority for almost a year, till transfer as Judge of the Delhi High Court. Nominated in July 2013 by the then Chief Justice of India for a week long training in Judicial Administration at the Civil Services College, Singapore. Appointed Judge of the Delhi High Court on 8th August 2016. Was Chairperson of the Delhi State Legal Services Authority. Sworn in as Chief Justice of Madras High Court on 5th April, 2017. Elevated as Judge of Supreme Court on 7th August, 2018. Due to retire on 24th September, 2022.

Name: Ms. Justice Indu Malhotra
Biodata: Born on March 14, 1956 in Bangalore. Did her schooling from Carmel Convent School, Delhi. Obtained Bachelors Degree in Political Science from Lady Shri Ram College in 1975, and then Masters Degree in Political Science in 1977 from Delhi University. Appointed as a Lecturer in Political Science in Miranda House College and Vivekanand College, Delhi University in 1978. Obtained post-graduate Diploma in Corporate Laws & Secretarial Practice from the Indian Law Institute in 1978-79. Completed her Bachelors Degree in Law from Delhi University in 1983. LEGAL PROFESSION Enrolled as an Advocate on January 12, 1983 with Bar Council of Delhi. Qualified as an Advocate-on-Record Examination in 1988 and was awarded the MukeshGoswami Memorial Prize for having topped the examination. 2nd woman to be designated as a Senior Advocate by the Supreme Court in 2007 after 30 years. Specialized in the law of Arbitration, and appeared as Counsel in various domestic and international commercial arbitrations both in India, and abroad. Appointed as a sole Arbitrator by various Arbitration Institutions. Certificate of the Diploma Course in International Commercial Arbitration by Chartered Institute of Arbitrators (CIArb.), England. Empanelled by SIAC as an Arbitrator in CIDC-SIAC from March 2006 to 2011. Appointed as a member of the High Level Committee constituted by the Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India in 2017 to review the working of Arbitration institutions in India, and to make recommendations for institutionalization of arbitration, and suggest legislative amendments to the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1966. Appointed as Amicus Curiae in various matters. Nominated by the Chief Justice of India in 2005 under the category of 'Eminent Persons' as a member of the General Council of the Gujarat National Law University established under the Gujarat National Law University Act. Member of the Board of Examiners of the Advocates-on-Record Examination constituted by the Supreme Court since 2013 to 2017. Was a Trustee of Save Life Foundation from inception till March 2018. Save life is an independent, non-governmental organization committed to taking various initiatives to prevent fatalities in road accidents, which include training of police personnel, framing of guidelines by the Supreme Court for protection of good Samaritans, etc. throughout the country. Save Life Foundation has been conferred various awards, including the Rolex Award for community service. Was a member of the Editorial Committee of the 'Nyaya Deep' official publication of the Supreme Court from August 2004 to 2013. Appointed to the National Legal Services Authority, constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. Was a member of the Supreme Court (Middle Income Group) Legal Aid Society from July 2005 to July 2008. Was a member of the Supreme Court Gender Sensitization and Internal Complaints Committee from November 2013 to 2017 In 2016, nominated as a Member of Central Council of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, a statutory body established under the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949. Represented India at the Convention on the Rights of the Child, conducted by the Commonwealth Secretariat in May 1988 at Dhaka, Bangladesh. Member of the Indo-British Legal Forum held in January, 2003 and March, 2008. ACADEMIC PURSUITS AND PUBLICATIONS Authored the 3rd Edition of the Commentary on the Law and Practice of Arbitration and Conciliation. Regularly invited by various Law Universities to deliver lectures including University of Delhi, National Academy of Legal Studies & Research NALSAR, Hyderabad, Gujarat National Law University, ILS Law College, Pune, Symbiosis College of Law, Pune and Amity University, Delhi.
LLB_Institutition: Faculty of Law, University of Delhi
Other_Bachelors_Institution: Lady Shri Ram College For Women

Name: MS. JUSTICE J. UMA DEVI
Court: High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad for the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh
Biodata: Born on 26.9.1959 at Ananthapur in Andhra Pradesh State to late Sri Javalakar Gnanoba Rao and late Smt. Javalakar Thulasibai. Graduated in Bachelor of Commerce having prosecuted in Sri Satya Sai Institute of Higher Learning, Ananthapur for the academic year 1979-1982. Did Bachelor of Law in Sri Krishna Devaraya University, Ananthapur during the academic year 1983-1986. Also did LL.M. in Annamalia University, Chennai by way of distance mode. Enrolled in Bar Council of Andhra Pradesh as an Advocate on 6.9.1986 and practised in District Courts, Ananthapur from 1987 onwards having been attached to the office of Senior Advocate Mr. Varada Rao. Selected and appointed as District Judge, Grade-II (Direct Recruitment) on 14.12.1996 and later became Prl. District Judge and worked at various places including Kurnool, Visakhapatnam, Warangal, Madanapalli, Mahaboonagar and Hyderabad. Worked as Chief Judge, City Small Causes Court, Hyderabad before elevation. Appointed and sworn in as Judge of High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad for the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh on 17.1.2017. Laid down office on 25.09.2021 on attaining the age of superannuation.
Other_Bachelors_Institution: Sri Satya Sai Institute of Higher Learning, Ananthapur

Name: Ms. Justice Jaishree Thakur
Biodata: Name : Hon'ble Ms. Justice Jaishree Thakur Date Of Birth : 24.07.1961 Educational Qualification : B.A., LL.B., LL.M. Date of Enrolment : 19.07.1986 Date of Elevation : 25.09.2014 Judge, Rajasthan High Court : 05.01.2015 Prof. Area of Specialization : Civil, Company, Services and Rent Law matters Was born on the 24h of July 1961 at Chandigarh. Her father was a Professor having taught both English Literature and Persian. Did her schooling from Sacred Heart School at Chandigarh and did her graduation from Government College for Women Chandigarh with History'Hons.) in 1st Division in the year 1981. Thereafter, did her Law from Punjab University, Chandigarh, in the year 1984 and LL.M. (Specialization in Company Law) in 1986 with 1st Division. Was enrolled as an Advocate in the year 1986 with Bar Council of Punjab & Haryana and started practice in the Punjab & Haryana High Court at Chandigarh. Was appointed as Deputy Advocate General Punjab in March 1992 and remained in office till November 1992. Had taught as Part Time Lecturer in the Law Department Punjab University for six years. Also remained as Additional Senior Standing Counsel for Chandigarh Administration. In her private practice, dealt mainly with civil and corporate matters. Has been a reporter with the Indian Law Reporter for a number of years and was appointed as Editor in 2013 and remained as such till her elevation. Has been awarded college colors for sports. Apart from sports was also involved in Theater both during college and after. Was elevated as Judge of the Punjab & Haryana High Court on 25th September 2014. Was transferred to Rajasthan High Court and assumed the charge on 5th January, 2015. Now her Lordship has been transferred to this Court and assumed the charge on 5th October, 2016.
LLB_Institutition: Punjab University, Department of Laws, Chandigarh

Name: Ms. Justice Nisha M. Thakore
Biodata: Born on 03.12.1975 at Ahmedabad. Initial schooling from Reubs Primary and High School, Ahmedabad. Cleared 12th Std. with Science Stream from N.R. Higher Secondary School, GLS, Ahmedabad, in March, 1993. Did Graduation in Bachelor of Science with Bio-Chemistry as a main subject from M.G. Science College, Gujarat University, Ahmedabad. Thereafter, did Master in Science with Bio-Chemistry from School of Science, Gujarat University, Ahmedabad and did Bachelor of Laws from I.M. Nanavati Law College, Ahmedabad. Simultaneously, worked as Quality Assurance Officer with West Coast Pharmaceutical Pvt. Co. and left the job to join legal field. Enrolled as an Advocate with Bar Council of Gujarat from September, 2002. Initially, attended City Civil Court matters under the guidance of Her father late Shri Mahendrabhai K. Thakore. On 12.09.2002, joined the office of learned Advocate Smt. Ketty Arun Mehta, had rich experience of matters related to the Land Laws and Service Laws. Simultaneously had gained experience through learned Advocate late Shri Arun Mehta, who had given opportunity to attend the few matters related to Taxation and Criminal Laws. In the year 2011, appointed as an Assistant Government Pleader, High Court of Gujarat. Had vast experience of attending various matters related mainly to Land Laws as well as matters pertaining to Service Laws, Labour Laws, Contempt of Courts. In the year 2016, appointed as Additional Public Prosecutor, High Court of Gujarat, whereby had occasions to deal with Criminal matters pertaining to Bail, Quashing, Criminal Appeals and Habeas Corpus. Also, briefly served as Panel Advocate for Mehsana District Panchayat, Liquidator of Gujarat State Petrofils Cooperative Limited (Company in Liquidation) and Sardar Sarovar Nigam Ltd. Had brief but rich experience of Service matters while representing the Office of Registrar, High Court of Gujarat and various District and Lower Courts since Year 2019. Elevated as Judge of High Court of Gujarat on 18.10.2021.

Biodata: Enrolled as an advocate in the year 1987 after finishing the law degree. Got post gradution degrees in Law, Master of Human Rights and Women Studies. Has been a member of Dindigul Bar Association and Practised in the District Courts of Dindigul in both Civil and Criminal side. Joined in Tamil Nadu State Judicial Service in the year 1995 as a Junior Division Civil Judge and worked in several places across Tamil Nadu in various capacities for 25 years. Has delivered judgements in sensational cases like Ayanavaram Child rape case and Kovilpatti Bomb Blast Case. Also functioned as the Registrar for Tamil Nadu State Human Rights Commission SHRC on deputation basis. Has been the Head for the 3 members Special Committee of SHRC for making field enquiry on the calamity that occurred on the Marina Beach during the Jalli Kattu Protest. Chosen as one among the two to represent India at Netherlands for a 3 week program on Protection of Human Rights conducted by the The Hague Academy of International Law, at The International Court of Justice, Peace Palace, The Hague in the year 1998. Has been the Vice-President for the Tamil Nadu Judges Association. Appointed as an Additional Judge of Madras High Court on 03.12.2020.,

Name: Ms. Justice Ritu Bahri
Biodata: Her Lordship was born on October 11, 1962 at Jalandhar. She belongs to a family of illustrious Lawyers. Her great grand-father Late Shri Karam Chand Bahri was a well known Lawyer of his times on the civil side. Her grand-father Late Shri Som Dutt Bahri also practiced Law on the civil side and was also Member Legislative Assembly, Punjab, from 1952 to 1957. Her father Hon'ble Mr. Justice Amrit Lal Bahri retired as Judge of Punjab & Haryana High Court in the year 1994. Her Lordship did her schooling from Carmel Convent School, Chandigarh, and graduation in Economics (Hons.) from Government College for Women, Chandigarh in the year 1982 in Ist Division. Thereafter, she did her Law from Punjab University, Chandigarh, in the year 1985 in Ist Divison. She was enrolled as an Advocate in the year 1986 with Bar Council of Punjab & Haryana and started practice in Punjab & Haryana High Court. She was appointed as Assistant Advocate General, Haryana, in March 1992. Thereafter, she was appointed as Deputy Advocate General, Haryana, in August 1999 and Senior Advocate General, Haryana, in December 2009. While reprsenting the State of Haryana, she handled several cases relating to Service matters, land Acquisition, Taxation, Revenue, Labour cases and MACT cases. She was elevated as Judge of the Punjab & Haryana High Court on August 16, 2010.
LLB_Institutition: Punjab University, Department of Laws, Chandigarh

Name: MS. JUSTICE ROHINI
Biodata: Hon'ble Ms. Justice G. Rohini was born on 14th April 1955 at Visakhapatnam, in Andhra Pradesh State, India. She was graduated in Science in the year 1976 from Osmania University and obtained degree in Law with First Class from the College of Law, Andhra University, Visakhapatnam., Enrolled as an Advocate on 18.12.1980 and joined the Office of Sri Koka Raghava Rao, Advocate, the then Chairman of Andhra Pradesh State Bar Council. She had the unique opportunity of participating actively in Legal Journalism. Initially she was the Reporter of Andhra Pradesh Law Journals of which Sri Koka Raghava Rao is the founder Chief Editor and in the year 1985 she became the Executive Editor of the said Journals.Actively practised mostly in the Andhra Pradesh High Court and also in the Administrative Tribunals and Civil Courts. Appeared in various types of Writ Petitions, Civil, Criminal, Labour and Service matters., Appointed as a Government Pleader in the High Court of Andhra Pradesh on 12.01.1995 and continued till she was elevated to the Bench. As a Government Pleader she was in charge of Departments of Food & Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs, Science & Technology, Environment, Irrigation and Command Area Development, Energy, Finance & Planning, Labour, Employment & Training from time to time., Appointed as Additional Judge of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh and sworn in as such on 25-06-2001. Appointed as a Permanent Judge on 31-07-2002. Appointed as Chief Justice of Delhi High Court and assumed charge as such on the forenoon of 21-04-2014.]

Name: Ms. Justice S. G. Gokani
Biodata: Born on 26th February 1961 at Jamnagar. Qualification: B.SC [Microbiology ], LL.B [ Special ] & LL.M [ Criminal ] As an advocate worked with various organizations for the cause of down trodden, women and children, as also for upholding the cause of environment. Served as part-time Lecturer at Shri K.P Shah Law College, Jamnangar and appointed and served as Member , District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum for nearly five years. Joined Judiciary directly in the cadre of District judges as a Judge, City Civil & Sessions Court, Ahmedabad on 10th July 1995 and presided over on many civil and criminal matters. After establishment of Special Court under the Anti-Terrorist Laws in the State of Gujarat, worked as a Special Judge for this Court and conducted important matters from 2003 to 2008. Worked as a Judge, Special Court C.B.I for the cases investigated by CBI. Deputed in March 2008 to the High Court of Gujarat as Registrar Recruitment for recruitment of Judicial officers upto the cadre of District Judges. Served also, as Registrar [IT & Infrastructure] for nearly 18 months, during which period, made presentation at different national forums, visiting Faculty Member at Gujarat State Judicial Academy and at other Academic Institutions. On 17th February 2011 – elevated as Additional Judge of the High Court of Gujarat and confirmed as permanent Judge on 28.01.2013.

Name: MS. JUSTICE S.V. MARUTHI
Biodata: Hon'ble Ms. Justice S.V. Maruthi was born on 24.11.1937 at Rajahmundry, East Godavari District. Educated B.Sc., from Nizam College, Hyderabad in the year 1958, LL.B. from Osmania University in the year 1960, LL.M. from Osmania University in 1970. Enrolled as an Advocate on 27.11.1961. Joined in the office of B.V. Ramanaran, Advocate. Worked as Junior to Justice Valluri Pardhasaradhi, Justice M. Krishna Rao, and Justice G. Venkata Rama Sastry also worked with V.R. Reddy. Joined in the Law Ministry on 04.08.1978. Appointed as Judicial Member on 16.01.1989. Appointed as Permanent Judge on 01.11.1992. Retired on 24.11.1999.]

Name: Ms. Justice Sangeeta K. Vishen
Biodata: Born on 30th December, 1969 at Mahudha Taluka, Kheda District. Did initial schooling at Valsad, and thereafter, completed Secondary and Higher Secondary school education from Firdaus Amrut School, Ahmedabad. After having obtained bachelor's degree in Commerce in the year 1991 and degree in Law in the year 1994, both from Gujarat University, Ahmedabad, got enrolled as an advocate with Bar Council of Gujarat from 12th August, 1994, and immediately thereafter, started practicing in the High Court of Gujarat. Was appointed as Assistant Government Pleader in the year 2003, attached with the learned Additional Advocate General, State of Gujarat, and subsequently in the year 2004, was appointed as Additional Public Prosecutor. From December, 2005 onwards, was assisting the learned Advocate General, State of Gujarat. In the said capacities, had appeared before the High Court of Gujarat, representing the State Government and its various Departments, Government Companies, Public Sector Establishments in different branches of law, including Constitutional, Civil, Service, Industrial and Company law. Elevated as Judge, High Court of Gujarat on 5th March, 2019.

Biodata: Mrs. Justice Sujata Vasant Manohar, B.Sc., B.L., Born on 28th August, 1934. Educated at Anandilal Podar High School, Bombay; Elphinstone College, Bombay, Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, U.K. And Lincoln's Inn, London. Enrolled Advocate on 14th February, 1958 at Bombay. Practised in the Bombay High Court on the Original Side. Appointed Assistant Government Pleader, City Civil Court, Bombay during 1970-71. Name: Ms. Justice Vaibhavi D. Nanavati
Biodata: Born on 15.11.1970 at Surat, Gujarat. She completed her Graduation in Arts from St. Xaviers College, Ahmedabad in 1992. She completed her Graduation in Law from Sir L.A. Shah Law College, Ahmedabad in 1995. She joined the bar in the year 1995. As an advocate she had conducted various matters pertaining to education laws, land laws, service laws and others. She had been on the panel of various statutory organizations being Medical Council of India, Central Board of Excise and Customs, Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, Gujarat University, State Bank of India and various others. She came to be appointed as Judge of the Gujarat High Court on 04.10.2020.

Name: N. B. SURYAWANSHI, J.
Biodata: Born on 30/05/1966. Completed schooling from Jai Hind High School, Dhule. Completed B.S.L. and L.L.B. Course from Symbiosis Law College, Pune. Enrolled as an Advocate on 05/08/1988. Started practice at District and Sessions Court, Dhule with Father Advocate B.P. Suryawanshi, a leading Criminal Lawyer. Earned experience of trial work by conducting trials, also conducted Sessions trials at Dhule. Shifted to Aurangabad High Court Bench in June, 1993 and joined chamber of Senior Shri R.N. Dhorde, Advocate. From 1996 onwards, started independent practice and handled Constitutional, Civil, Criminal, Labour and Service Law matters. Conduced two death sentence confirmation cases. Was on the panel of Bombay High Court at Aurangabad Bench, represented State Bank of India, various Municipal Councils, Municipal Corporations, District Central Co-operative Bank, Zilla Parishad etc. Was on A panel Advocate of State of Maharashtra. Was unanimous President of Aurangabad High Court Advocates Association for the year 2011-12 Elevated as Additional Judge on 23/08/2019.

Name: NELAVOY DHINAKAR, B.A, B.L.
Biodata: Nelavoy dhinakar, B.A, B.L. chief justice of the jharkhand high court Nelavoy dhinakar, B.A, B.L., was born on june 10, 1944. he was enrolled as an advocate on january 31, 1968. he practised in the madras high court in criminal and constitutional cases involving preventive detention laws. He worked as an additional public prosecutor and as a defence lawyer. He worked as government advocate in the high court from june 17, 1988 to march 22, 1989. he was appointed as a special public prosecutor to conduct important cases. He was appointed as a permanent judge of the madras high court on october 17, 1994 and transferred to the kerala high court on november 30, 1994. he was transferred back to the madras high court on march 5, 1999. he was appointed as the chief justice of the jharkhand high court on december 4, 2005. retired on june 10, 2006.

Name: NITIN JAMDAR, J.
Biodata: Graduated in Commerce and Law from the University of Mumbai. Practiced in the Bombay High Court. Elevated as a Judge of the Bombay High court on 23 January 2012.

Name: NITIN W. SAMBRE, J.
Biodata: Born on 19th December, 1967 at Nagpur. Completed his schooling from Somalwar High School and Shivaji Science College. Graduated in Law in the year 1992 from University College of Law, Nagpur. Being a Sportsman, represented State of Maharashtra in National Tournaments. Was elected as President of the Students Union of the University College of Law, Nagpur in 1991. Enrolled as an Advocate on 25th August, 1992. Started legal career with then Senior Advocate Shri Sharad A. Bobde, (now Honourable Judge, Supreme Court of India). Practised in the High Court of Bombay, Nagpur on Civil, Writ and Criminal sides. Was the Secretary of the High Court Bar Associ ation, Nagpur for 2004-07. Represented Governor of Maharashtra in the High Court Bench at Nagpur. Was appointed as Government Pleader and Public Prosecutor on 1st September, 2007. Was Counsel for Nagpur Improvement Trust, Special Counsel for Forest Department and Scheduled Tribes Caste Certificate Verification Committee. Was Standing Counsel for Public Undertakings such as Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd., Indian Oil Corporation and Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd, etc. Represented statutory bodies such as various Municipal Corporations and Councils. Also represented companies like Tata Sons, Godrej, etc. Elevated as a Judge of Bombay High Court on 6th January, 2014.

Name: P. B. VARALE, J.
Biodata: Also worked as Assistant Government Pleader and Additional Public Prosecutor, High Court Bench at Aurangabad AND Additional Standing Counsel for Union Of India. Elevated at Bombay High Court on 18/07/2008.

Name: P. D. NAIK, J.
Biodata: Born on 30th April 1962 at Goa. Completed his graduation from St.Xavier's College, Goa in 1983. Graduated in Law in the year 1986 from Siddharth Law College, Mumbai. Did his LL.M. from University of Bombay in 1988. Enrolled as an Advocate on 21st July 1986. Joined the chambers of Shri Shirish Gupte, Senior Advocate and former Additional Solicitor General. Initially started practice in all Courts in Mumbai and handled both civil as well as criminal litigation. Subsequently specialized in criminal matters. Appeared in matters relating to prisoners' rights, illegal detention, preventive detention, parole, furlough and matters of premature release and remission. Was a member of the Committee appointed by Bombay High Court to look into the plight of prisoners and conditions in prisons in the State of Maharashtra. As a member of said committee, headed by Senior Advocates, visited several jails in Maharashtra and after inerviewing a number of under-trials and convicts/prisoners, drafted a report, relating to the conditions in prison and recommended improvements thereto. Was empanelled as Senior Advocate by Mumbai Municipal Corporation and represented the Corporation in its various proceedings. Was Honorary Lecturer between 1987 and 1988 at Siddharth Law College, Mumbai. Was engaged as a Part Time Professor at Jitendra Chauhan College of Law, Mumbai. Was a visiting Professor for the LL.M. course (1st and 2nd years), Bombay University, at Mumbai between 2011 and 2012. Delivered lectures on Criminal Law and Criminal Administration. Elevated as Additional Judge of Bombay High Court on 17th March 2016.
LLM_Institutition: University Department of Law, University of Mumbai

Name: PRITHVIRAJ K. CHAVAN, J.
Biodata: Born on 22nd February, 1963. Completed schooling at various places as father was Doctor in Central Railway. Did B.Sc. Zoology from Shivaji University, Kolhapur in 1983. Worked as Development officer in Life Insurance Corporation of India. Obtained LL.B. Degree from Nagpur University in the year 1987 and started Practice in the office of late Hon'ble Shri Justice B.U.Wahane in the High Court of Judicature Bombay, Bench at Nagpur as well as in the District Court, Nagpur from 1987 till 1989. Appointed as Assistant Public Prosecutor, Registrar of Joint Stock Companies, Sub Registrar at the Union Territory of Diu in 1989. Appointed as Civil Judge, Jr. Dn. & JMFC in June 1992 and posted at Yavatmal. Promoted in the cadre of District Judge, Amravati in the month of March 2002. Worked as Additional District and Sessions Judge at Amaravati, Bhandara, Gangakhed and Basmat Distt Parbhani. Worked as Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bombay from June 2008 to September 2009. Appointed as Registrar Vigilance, (Finance & Budget), Protocol in the High Court, Bombay, from 2009 to 2012. Was a Judge of City Civil and Sessions Court, Bombay From 1st March, 2012 to February 2014. Dealt with several matters as a Special Judge under MCOCA, POTA and NIA. Delivered a judgment as a Special Judge under the National Investigation Agency Act wherein the accused were convicted for having found in possession of Fake Indian Currency Notes manufactured in the neighbouring country. Appointed as Chief Judge, Small Causes Court, Bombay, from February 2014 to February 2016. Transferred to Amravati as Principal District & Sessions Judge with effect from 7.3.2016. Transferred to Pune as Principal District and Sessions Judge in the month of September 2016. Delivered Lecture on evidentiary value of Forensic Science, Medical evidence and role of Experts in Indian Law at Tata Institute of Social Science, Mumbai. Attended and participated in the International Conference of Forensic Nano Technology held at Forensic Science University, Gandhinagar, Gujrat on 25.3.2011. Appointed as a Member for the Board of Studies for Forensic Science at University of Mumbai. Keenly interested in Forensic Criminology. During college days, participated in cultural and social activities. Has Been awarded with Black Belt (One Dan) in karate from Shyorin Ryu - Japan. Keenly interested in mouth organ and violin. Elevated as Additional Judge of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay on 5th June, 2017.

Name: Pushpendra Singh Bhati
Biodata: Hon'ble Dr. Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati Date Of Birth : 21.09.1970 Official Address : Rajasthan High Court, Jaipur. Educational Qualification : BA, LL.B., LL.M. in Mercantile Law., Ph.D. in “Promotion & Seniority in Public Employment, its Changing Dimensions and Role of Supreme Court.” Date of Enrolment : 1992 Date of Elevation : 16.11.2016 Prof Area of Specialization : Writ Jurisdiction (Service & Misc. both), Revenue, Election, Mining, Education, Panchayati Raj, Criminal and misc. matters including Public Interest Litigation. Practiced in Rajasthan High Court, Jodhpur, mainly in Writ Jurisdiction spanning across Service Laws, Public Interest Litigation, Election, Revenue, Mining, Education, Panchayati Raj, Family, Criminal and misc. matters. Was Additional Advocate General, Raj. High Court, Jodhpur from 13.10.2008 to 29.12.2008 and 06.01.2014 till elevation. Remained Panel Lawyer for Kendriya Vidhyalaya Sangthan, OIL & Natural Gas Corporation, Labour Department (Govt. of Raj.), Ayurved Department (Govt. of Raj.). Represented Reserve Bank of India, Jai Narain Vyas University, Jodhpur and many other bodies. Was Standing Counsel for Indian Railways for 16 years. Elected as Member, Bar Council of Rajasthan from 2009-2015. Elected as President, Raj. High Court Lawyers Association 2011-2013 & General Secretary, Raj. High Court Advocates Association in 2001. Trained Mediator of Raj. High Court. Was Visiting Faculty at his alma-mater Faculty of Law, Jai Narain Vyas University, Jodhpur for 19 years (1997 to 2016) and Visiting Faculty of National Law University, Jodhpur for one year. Is Member of Executive Committee of Indian Law Institute (Raj. Chapter). Member, Supreme Court Bar Association since 1992. Excellent Horse Rider, Swimmer, Shooter, a Solo Glider Pilot, ParaSailor; participated in many adventurous activities with NCC and has A, B & C Certificates. Participated in several National Conferences and Television debates and deliberated on myriad issues of importance for the Administration of Justice. Was Vice President of Students Union, Law Faculty, JNV University in 1990-91.

Name: R. G. AVACHAT, J.
Biodata: Born on 15th March, 1964. Completed education up to graduation i.e. B.Com. at Shirur Ghodnadi, District Pune. Did LL.B.(First Class throughout) from I.L.S. Law College, Pune in 1987. Enrolled as an Advocate with Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa in June, 1987. Practised at District Court, Pune and the Court of Civil Judge, Junior Division and Judicial Magistrate, First Class at Ghodnadi. Joined judiciary as Civil Judge, Junior Division and Judicial Magistrate, First Class in May, 1992. Promoted as Ad-hoc Additional District Judge in October, 2003 and then as District Judge in January, 2008. Served as Principal District Judge, Kolhapur from May, 2015 to July, 2017 and thereafter, served as Registrar Vigilance, High Court of Judicature at Bombay. Elevated as Judge of Bombay High Court on 11th October, 2018.

Name: R. I. CHAGLA, J.
Biodata: Born on 22nd October 1969 at Mumbai. Completed his graduation from H.R. College of Commerce and Economics, Mumbai University in 1991. Graduated in Law in the year 1993 from University of Cambridge - Downing College. Enrolled as an Advocate with the Bar Council of Maharashtra & Goa on 5th July 1993. Joined the Chambers of Senior Counsel Mr. Darius Khambata (Former Additional Solicitor General and Advocate General). Practiced as Counsel in the Hon'ble Bombay High Court for over 23 years and also appeared in the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. Appointed on the Union Panel (Senior Counsel Group - 1) in November, 2009 and represented the Central Government in cases under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, FEMA, NDPS Act etc. Appointed on the State Government Panel - Panel 'A' on 21st September, 2013. During practice as Counsel appeared in Civil, Constitutional, Commercial, Corporate, Intellectual Property, Taxation and Testamentary cases. Appeared and also acted as Arbitrator in several Arbitrations. Elevated as Additional Judge of Bombay High Court on 5th June 2017.

Name: R. N. LADDHA, J.
Biodata: Hon'ble Shri Justice Laddha did his LL.B. from the University College of Law, Nagpur affiliated to the then Nagpur University and enrolled as an Advocate in the year 1989. Practiced mainly on Civil and Criminal side. He joined Judiciary as a Direct District Judge from Bar in the year 2008 and since then has worked twice as Judge, City Civil and Sessions Court, Mumbai; Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kolhapur; Principal District and Sessions Judge, Latur and Principal District and Sessions Judge, Satara. Also worked in the Registry of the Bombay High Court on various positions as Registrar Inspection and Registrar Vigilance. Elevated as Additional Judge of Bombay High Court on 25th June 2021.

Biodata: He was on the Senior Counsel Panel of Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai for last several years and has appeared in large number of matters representing Municipal Corporation in Bombay High Court. Joined as Additional Judge of the Bombay High Court on 23rd January, 2012.

Name: Rajeev Ranjan Prasad
Biodata: Born on 5th September, 1966 in the family of Smt. Laxmi Singh and Shri Umesh Prasad Singh, he got his early school education at Patna, Graduated in Commerce from Patna University and went to Hansraj College, Delhi University where he did one year Special Certificate Course in Commerce. Having secured First Position in First Division in the said course which was popularly known as ‘Bridge Course’ he got admission in the Post Graduation Program in Commerce in the Delhi School of Economics, but later on left the said programme and joined LL.B programme in Delhi University to make career in law. Having passed out LL.B. from Campus Law Centre, University of Delhi in the year 1991, started his practice in Patna High Court. Learnt basics of legal profession in the chambers of his father Shri Umesh Prasad Singh who is a Senior Advocate in the High Court at Patna and has his Chambers at Ranchi as well. After starting practice in Patna High Court on 26.08.1991, got occasion to assist a number of senior Advocates at the Bar in Patna, Jharkhand , Calcutta and Delhi High Court and visited several Hon'ble High Courts in India to represent his clients. Established his offices in the State of Jharkhand at Ranchi as also at Kolkata. Being an out Station member of the Supreme Court Bar Association got opportunities to appear in several cases in the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. Also appeared in Company Law Board, B.I.F.R., A.A.I.F.R at Delhi and National Company Law Tribunal at Kolkata. Worked for several Central as well as State Government's organization in the capacity of Retainer or Additional Retainer Advocate. At the time of elevation to the Bench, he was working for LIC of India, Central Bank of India, Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority, Bihar State Industrial Development Corporation, Infrastructure Development Authority, Bihar State Tourism Development Corporation and was also representing the Economic Offences Unit, Bihar Patna as a Law Officer. His area of practice was mostly in the Company Matters, Contract, Commercial, Service and Civil Matters.
LLB_Institutition: Faculty of Law, University of Delhi

Name: RAVINDRA V. GHUGE, J.
Biodata: Son of Mrs.Meena and Prof. V.B.Ghuge (former Vice-Chancellor), did schooling SSC from elite Saint Xavier's High School Kolhapur. Completed five year Law course from Chh.Shahaji Law College, Kolhapur & M.P.Law College, Aurangabad, in April / May 1990. Stood 1st in the college and Marathwada University in the Moot Court competition in 1989. Represented the University in the Inter-University National Moot Court Competition at Simla, H.P., in October 1989. Joined the Bar in 1990 and started practice in the Bombay High Court and Industrial / Labour Courts, initially representing workers and unions in about 2000 cases. Has conducted cases for about 250 Industries including many MNCs and private Large Scale Industries in the High Court, Labour & Industrial Courts, Tribunals, etc. Bajaj Auto Limited, Colgate-Palmolive, Carlsberg, Taj Hotels, Skoda Auto India Pvt.Ltd., Siemens Ltd., Wipro Ltd., Johnson & Johnson, Endress + Hauser (Swedish Co.), Goodyear Tyres, Lombardini Koehler (US Co.), Hindustan Lever, Kamalnayan Bajaj Hospital, Mahyco Seeds, Wockhardt Ltd., Bar Council of India, etc. were some of his prominent clients. Appeared before many High Courts and its Benches. Petition filed by him concerning ESIC hospitals led to the formation of a Special Committee of Doctors to recommend improvements in infrastructural facilities and medical amenities in the ESIC Hospital. Was Contributory Professor for the PG LL.M. Course (1st & 2nd years), Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University, Aurangabad (2005-2006 till 2007-2008). Delivered lectures on Industrial, Labour & Service Law at various seminars. Contributed articles to journals for NIPM, Silver Jubilee souvenir of the Aurangabad Bench of Bombay High Court and Bar Association of Industrial Lawyers, Aurangabad. Was Secretary (05 years) and President (July 2010-December 2011) of the Bar Association of Industrial Lawyers, Aurangabad. A keen Cricket player, represented his school, Law College, District and the Zone in Jasdanwala State Tournament. Also represented the District Court & High Court teams in the Advocates Trophy, Maharashtra. Elevated as Judge of the Bombay High Court on 21/06/2013.
LLB_Institutition: Chh.Shahaji Law College, Kolhapur & M.P.Law College, Aurangabad

Name: Rekha Borana
Biodata: Hon'ble Ms. Justice Rekha Borana Date Of Birth : 02.12.1973 Educational Qualification : B.A., LL.M. Official Address : Rajasthan High Court, Jodhpur. Date of Elevation : 29.10.2021 Had been selected for the Rajasthan Administrative Services in the year 1997 but did not join the services and chose the legal profession. Practised before Subordinate Courts and High Court on the civil side with specialization in Arbitration matters. Was elected as the first Woman General Secretary of the Rajasthan High Court Advocates Association, Jodhpur. Was appointed as the Additional Advocate General for the State of Rajasthan on 8th January 2019 & worked as same till the date of elevation. Have the honour to be the first Woman Judge of the Rajasthan High Court from the Bar.

Name: S. C. MORE, J.
Biodata: Born on 07th April, 1966. Had school education at Pethe High School, Nashik. Completed Graduation in Science faculty at R. Y. K. College of Science, Nashik, Pune University. Completed Law education in N.B.T. Law College, Nashik. During the service period, completed Diploma course in Cyber Crimes in Government Law College, Mumbai. Started practice in Nashik District Court and also some of the Mofussil Courts therein. Worked on Civil, Criminal and Revenue sides. Got selected as direct District Judge in the year 2008 and initially posted at Bhandara as District Judge-1. Thereafter transferred to Small Causes Court at Mumbai as an Additional Chief Judge in the year 2011. Subsequently, in the year 2012, posted as City Civil Judge and Additional Sessions Judge, City Civil Court Mumbai at Dindoshi. Thereafter worked as District Judge-1 and Additional Sessions Judge at Bhusawal and then got promoted as Principal District Judge, Yeotmal. Also served as 1st Additional Principal Judge, City Civil Court Mumbai at Dindoshi. Then posted as Chief Judge, Small Causes Court, Mumbai. Just before elevation, appointed as Principal District Judge, Nagpur on 1st July, 2021. A sportsperson having keen interest in Cricket and also represented Science College in intercollegiate cricket tournaments. Elevated as an Additional Judge of the Bombay High Court on 21st October, 2021.
Other_Bachelors_Institution: R. Y. K. College of Science, Nashik, Pune University

Name: S. D. KULKARNI, J.
Biodata: Graduated in Commerce (Hons.) from G.A. College of Commerce, Sangli. Completed LL.B. in the year 1984 from N.S. Law College, Sangli. Did LL.M. from Bharti Vidyapeeth, Pune and Diploma in Cyber Law (D.I.C.L.) from Government Law College, Mumbai and enrolled as an Advocate with Bar Council of Maharashtra & Goa in the year 1985. Practiced at various places in Sangli District and joined judiciary in the year 1990. Promoted as Addl.District Judge in the year 2002. Worked as Registrar Personnel and Registrar Judicial at Principal seat Bombay from 2013 to 2015. Appointed as Principal District & Sessions Judge, Ahmednagar and worked from the year 2015 to 13th July 2017. Worked as Member Secretary, Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority from 14th July 2017 to 13th January 2020. Elevated as Judge of Bombay High Court on 14th January 2020.

Name: S. G. DIGE, J.
Biodata: Born on 3rd August, 1971. Completed graduation at Dayanand Science College, Latur in Micro-Biology. Completed law in Dayanand Law College, Latur. Became President of District Bar Association, Latur in 2005. Got prize in Chess on Advocates State Level Competition. Represented the District Bar Association, Latur in State Level Cricket Tournament. Got selected as District Judge in 2008. Worked as CBI Special Judge, the Joint Charity Commissioner, Pune, the Principal District Judge, Ratnagiri, the Charity Commissioner, Maharashtra, Mumbai, the Registrar (Inspection-I) of Bombay High Court, Member Secretary, Maharashtra. State Legal Services Authority and thereafter worked as the Registrar General, Bombay High Court. Elevated as Additional Judge of Bombay High Court on 25th June,2021.

Name: S. G. MEHARE, J.

Enrolled as an Advocate with Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa on 31st December, 1988. Practised at District and Sessions Court at Akola, Amravati, Washim and Buldana on civil, criminal and revenue side. Joined Judiciary as District Judge on 2nd May, 2008. Posted as Principal District & Sessions Judge at Dadra, Nagar Haveli (U.T.) & Daman (U.T.), Gadchiroli, Nanded, Aurangabad and Nagpur. Also posted as Charity Commissioner of the State of Maharashtra. Elevated as Additional Judge of the Bombay High Court on 25th June, 2021.

Biodata: Born on 13th November, 1965 at Kalyan, District Thane Maharashtra in a reputed and renowned family. Studied in V.P. M's Bedekar College of Commerce and Thane Law College, both affiliated to Mumbai University, and took B. Com. and LL. B. Degrees in 1986 and 1989 respectively. Held the briefs for the Co-operative Scheduled Banks, namely the Kalyan Janata Sahakari Bank and Dombivali Nagari Sahakari Bank. bTopped the Merit List of the 2007 Batch as a direct District Judge. Name: S.B. SHUKRE, J.
Biodata: Hon'ble Shri Justice Shukre graduated from Pune University in 1980, and did his LL.B. in 1983 from Dr. Punjabrao Deshmukh Law College, Amravati affiliated to the then Nagpur University. Name: Sh. Justice Aftab Alam
Biodata: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Aftab Alam was born in Patna on April 19th, 1948 where he completed his School and College Education. Enrolled as an Advocate on 27.03.1973. Name: Sh. Justice B. C. Patel
Biodata: BABULAL CHANDULAL PATEL, Born on 07.08.1943 at Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Obtained degree of B.A. (Hons.) with Economics in 1963. Obtained LL.B. degree and also M.A. degree with Economics and Politics from Gujarat University in 1967. Enrolled as an Advocate on 05.04.1968. Started practice as an Advocate in the City Civil Court, Ahmedabad from 1968. Shifted his venue of practice to Gujarat High Court from 1970 onwards. Joined the Chamber of Well-known Criminal Side Advocate, Late Mr. H.K. Thakore and actively assisted and conducted with him many important Sessions Cases and Criminal appeals. Practiced independently as an Advocate in the High Court of Gujarat from 1981. Practiced in Civil, Constitutional and Criminal matters. Has represented Gujarat Electricity Board for 10 years in various courts. Has keen interest in education and has worked as Professor of Law in various colleges for about 15 years. Elevated to the Bench of Gujarat High Court as Permanent Judge on 21.06.1990. As Judge of Gujarat High Court, his lordship delivered landmark judgments particularly on town planning and building activities in urban areas. The celebrated judgments delivered by his Lordship paved way for removal of encroachments for public places and installation of safety devices in high-rise buildings. These landmark judgments of his Lordship were widely appreciated by general public. Was Acting Chief Justice of Gujarat High Court from 05.03.2002 to 16.03.2002. Elevated as Chief Justice, High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and took oath on 15.05.2002. Transferred as Chief Justice of Delhi High Court. Took oath as Chief Justice of Delhi High Court on 05.03.2003.
Other_Masters_Degree: M.A. degree with Economics and Politics

Name: Sh. Justice Badar Durrez Ahmed
Biodata: Born on 16th March, 1956 in Shillong Meghalaya. Studied in St Edmund's College, Shillong, (1962-1966) and St Columba's High School, New Delhi (1966-1971). Passed the Indian School Certificate Examination in 1971-1972. Was selected for the National Science Talent Scholarship (1972). However, took up Economics Hons and graduated from St Stephen's College, Delhi University in 1975. Passed Tripos in Economics Examination from Trinity College, Cambridge University, U.K. in 1977 and obtained the B.AHons and M.A. Degrees. Was Lecturer in Economics for B.A.Hons Second and Final Year students in St Stephen's College, Delhi (1977-1979). At the same time, was also studying for the LLB Degree which he received in 1980 from Delhi University. Enrolled as an Advocate on 5.9.1980 with the Bar Council of Delhi and started practice in the Supreme Court of India and Delhi High Court. Initially joined the chamber of Shri Siddhartha Shanker Ray, Bar-at-Law (Senior Advocate) for about three years. Thereafter, practiced law independently. In 1986 he set up a law firm under the name of “Lawyers Associated”. Was partner in the firm till March, 2000. Thereafter, practiced in the Supreme Court and other High Courts as counsel and also advised on various aspects of law relating to finance, companies, properties, banking, contracts and other areas of commercial and civil law. Also has a keen interest in Personal Laws including Muslim Personal Law and has written several articles in this connection. Has contributed the section on “Deeds and other instruments” for Halsbury's Law of India. He is keenly interested in computers and knows several computer programming languages including Assembly, C Basic, Visual Basic and dialects of Dbase (including Clipper) and has written two stand-alone accounting software packages for lawyers: ACT-C and ACT-S. Till his elevation as an additional Judge of the Delhi High Court on 20th December, 2002, he was also the Secretary of Ghalib Institute, New Delhi. He is a keen sportsman and played Cricket and Football for the school. Was member of the St Stephen's College Tennis Team and played Tennis and Squash for Trinity College, Cambridge, U.K. Appointed as Chief Justice of High Court of Jammu & Kashmir vide notification No.K.13021/01/2017-US.II dated 24th March,2017 and took oath of office on 1st April, 2017.
LLB_Institutition: Faculty of Law, University of Delhi

Name: Sh. Justice Bansi Lal Bhat
Biodata: Justice Bhat was born in remote village Arihal in Pulwama district. After passing his matriculation from Government High School, Hawal, he graduated from Amar Singh College, Srinagar and obtained his Law Degree from University of Kashmir. He was enrolled as pleader with Bar Association, Srinagar on 15th January, 1975. He practiced in Civil, Criminal and Revenue Courts until selection in KCS Judicial. He joined as Munsiff on 17th November, 1982 and was promoted as Sub Judge on 29th June, 1989. Later, he served as CJM, Jammu till his induction in Higher Judicial Service in August 1999. He also served as Principal District and Sessions Judge in both capital cities of Jammu and Srinagar besides at Poonch, Reasi and Kathua. He also served as Presiding Officer of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Jammu, besides serving for two tenures as Special Judge Anti Corruption Jammu and was appointed as Special Judge of the newly created Anti Corruption Court for trial of CBI cases on 18th August, 2011 where he served till his elevation. He contributed to development of law by delivering many landmark judgments and settled thousands of disputes as Presiding Officer of the Permanent Lok Adalat. He regularly contributed to State Judicial Academy newsletter and raised standard of legal education by delivering lectures in State Judicial Academy and Faculty of Law, University of Jammu. He was appointed as Additional Judge of J'amp;K State High Court on 8th March, 2013 and appointed as permanent Judge of the State High Court on 26th September, 2014. During his tenure, he delivered so many reportable judgments.

Name: Sh. Justice Barin Ghosh

On transfer to the High Court of Sikkim he took oath on April 13, 2010 as Chief Justice of the High Court of Sikkim.

Name: Sh. Justice Bawa Singh Walia

November 1, 2012, till elevation as Additional Judge of the Punjab and Haryana High Court on September 25, 2014. His Lordship on transfer took oath as Additional Judge of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir on 12.02.2015.

Name: Sh. Justice Bhawani Singh
Biodata: Born on 28.03.1944. He joined the legal profession and practiced in the Himachal Pradesh High Court and Supreme Court since 1968. Name: Sh. Justice F. M. Ibrahim Kalifulla
Biodata: Hon'ble Thiru. Justice Fakkir Mohamed Ibrahim Kalifulla. The learned Judge is the son of Late Thiru. Justice M. Fakkir Mohamed and was born on 23.07.1951. He hails from Karaikudi, Sivagangai District, Tamil Nadu and was enrolled as an Advocate on 20.08.1975. He was an active Labour Law Practitioner as Partner of the Lawyer's Firm called M/s. T.S. Gopalan & Co., and appeared for various Public and Private Sector Undertakings, Nationalised and Scheduled Banks. He was the Standing Counsel for the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board. On 02.03.2000, His Lordship was appointed as Permanent Judge of the Madras High Court. After assumption of office, the learned Judge has rendered very many landmark Judgments. In one case relating to election to a local body, namely, the Chennai City Corporation, sitting in a Division Bench, the learned Judge rendered a dissenting Judgment holding that the election in respect of 99 wards was liable to be set aside. The matter was referred to a third Judge and the third Judge also confirmed the view of Justice F.M.Ibrahim Kalifulla. Enthralled by the verdict of the learned Judge, there was widespread appreciation from all quarters. To quote a few, there was an article written by a retired conscientious bureaucrat of the Indian Administrative Service, which would be of worth mentioning. The said article appeared in ‘NEWS TODAY’ dated 13.1.2007 under the caption “ A MOMENT OF INFAMY FOR TAMILNADU GOVERNMENT”. It will be appropriate to quote what the author said in his article. “Through his judgment, Mr. Justice Kalifulla has given cubic content to the immortal words of Justice Felix Frankfurter: ‘Judges are not merely the habitations of bloodless categories of the law which pursue their pre-destined ends’. Instead of taking a sterile, bloodless and neutrally neutral view between good and evil, he has categorically declared:’ He has referred to the word of caution given by the Supreme Court of India to the effect that successful candidates who had resorted to foul methods should not be allowed to reap the benefits. He has also stated that he was convinced that ‘there was an extreme and extraordinary situation’, which warranted an extraordinary remedy in view of the magnitude of the situation. He has concluded that it would be wholly inappropriate if fresh elections were not ordered to a majority of the wards. By his verdict setting aside the civic elections in 99 wards out of 155 wards, Mr. Justice Kalifulla has demonstrated that another great American Judge and Jurist Benjamin N Cardozo (1870-1938) was absolutely right when he stated: ‘The great tides and currents which engulf the rest of men, do not turn aside in their course, and pass the judges by”. Appreciating the uncompromised stand taken by the learned Judge on the Corporation Polls, the Editor of the Madras Law Journal has expressed his view in the following words, which is reported in (2007) 1 MLJ Page 1, which read as under: “Whatever be the ultimate majority opinion that might emerge, it fills us with pride that a judge obtains a special eulogical mention in the Press for what it perceives to be correct decision. Praiseful references are made in obituary columns of farewell occasions. ‘When they come, when the judge is still in the Bench, not merely from a lawyer, who may have an axe to grind, but from the press, it is a defining moment for the judiciary itself.” One other landmark judgment delivered by the learned Judge was relating to introduction of Vedic Astrology as a course of Scientific study in the Indian Universities which had the seal of approval of the Supreme Court. When a challenge was made in the High Court in a writ petition, the learned Judge declined to interfere with the move of the State. In the Judgment reported in 2004-4-L.W.195 (Dr.K.Natarajan, Director, Dr.K.N..Study Centre for Humanism V. The Union of India represented by its Secretary to the Human Resources Department, New Delhi and another), the learned Judge expressed his views in the following words: “…..The very purpose of imparting education is to gain knowledge and also education is stated to be the teacher of a teacher. Therefore, there should be every scope for making a study on very many subjects in order to enrich one's craving for knowledge. Any such attempt from any quarters in furtherance of that pursuit, in my opinion should not, therefore, be stultified. ……By introducing the subject of Vedic Astrology either as a science subject or as an arts subject or under any other category, it will have to held that the same would only help the pupil to gain knowledge in that particular subject. ……When it is for the pupil concerned to select any particular field or subject in furtherance of his future career, merely because the subject has got its basic origin traceable to some cult, it cannot be held that the same would only result in propagation of a particular religion. On that footing, it cannot be held that there should be a ban on introduction of that subject as a course of scientific study.” The said view of the learned Judge was approved by the Hon'ble Supreme Court when a similar challenge came up for consideration before the Hon'ble Supreme Court. It is also reported in 2004-4 L.W.197. While approving the view of the Learned Judge, the Hon'ble Supreme Court referred in detail the point of view expressed by the Learned Judge in paragraph 16 of the judgment. Transferred to High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and assumed charge of Office on 24.02.2011. Appointed as Acting Chief Justice of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir on 07.04.2011. Took oath as Chief Justice of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir on 18.09.2011. Elevated as Judge, Supreme Court of India on 2nd April, 2012.

He hails from Karaikudi, Sivagangai District, Tamil Nadu and was enrolled as an Advocate on 20.08.1975. He was an active Labour Law Practitioner as Partner of the Lawyer's Firm called M/s. T.S. Gopalan & Co., and appeared for various Public and Private Sector Undertakings, Nationalised and Scheduled Banks. He was the Standing Counsel for the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board. On 02.03.2000, His Lordship was appointed as Permanent Judge of the Madras High Court. After assumption of office, the learned Judge has rendered very many landmark Judgments. In one case relating to election to a local body, namely, the Chennai City Corporation, sitting in a Division Bench, the learned Judge rendered a dissenting Judgment holding that the election in respect of 99 wards was liable to be set aside. The matter was referred to a third Judge and the third Judge also confirmed the view of Justice F.M.Ibrahim Kalifulla. Enthralled by the verdict of the learned Judge, there was widespread appreciation from all quarters. To quote a few, there was an article written by a retired conscientious bureaucrat of the Indian Administrative Service, which would be of worth mentioning. The said article appeared in ‘NEWS TODAY’ dated 13.1.2007 under the caption “ A MOMENT OF INFAMY FOR TAMILNADU GOVERNMENT”. It will be appropriate to quote what the author said in his article. “Through his judgment, Mr. Justice Kalifulla has given cubic content to the immortal words of Justice Felix Frankfurter: ‘Judges are not merely the habitations of bloodless categories of the law which pursue their pre-destined ends’. Instead of taking a sterile, bloodless and neutrally neutral view between good and evil, he has categorically declared:’ He has referred to the word of caution given by the Supreme Court of India to the effect that successful candidates who had resorted to foul methods should not be allowed to reap the benefits. He has also stated that he was convinced that ‘there was an extreme and extraordinary situation’, which warranted an extraordinary remedy in view of the magnitude of the situation. He has concluded that it would be wholly inappropriate if fresh elections were not ordered to a majority of the wards. By his verdict setting aside the civic elections in 99 wards out of 155 wards, Mr. Justice Kalifulla has demonstrated that another great American Judge and Jurist Benjamin N Cardozo (1870-1938) was absolutely right when he stated: ‘The great tides and currents which engulf the rest of men, do not turn aside in their course, and pass the judges by”. Appreciating the uncompromised stand taken by the learned Judge on the Corporation Polls, the Editor of the Madras Law Journal has expressed his view in the following words, which is reported in (2007) 1 MLJ Page 1, which read as under: “Whatever be the ultimate majority opinion that might emerge, it fills us with pride that a judge obtains a special eulogical mention in the Press for what it perceives to be correct decision. Praiseful references are made in obituary columns of farewell occasions. ‘When they come, when the judge is still in the Bench, not merely from a lawyer, who may have an axe to grind, but from the press, it is a defining moment for the judiciary itself.” One other landmark judgment delivered by the learned Judge was relating to introduction of Vedic Astrology as a course of Scientific study in the Indian Universities which had the seal of approval of the Supreme Court. When a challenge was made in the High Court in a writ petition, the learned Judge declined to interfere with the move of the State. In the Judgment reported in 2004-4-L.W.195 (Dr.K.Natarajan, Director, Dr.K.N..Study Centre for Humanism V. The Union of India represented by its Secretary to the Human Resources Department, New Delhi and another), the learned Judge expressed his views in the following words: “…..The very purpose of imparting education is to gain knowledge and also education is stated to be the teacher of a teacher. Therefore, there should be every scope for making a study on very many subjects in order to enrich one's craving for knowledge. Any such attempt from any quarters in furtherance of that pursuit, in my opinion should not, therefore, be stultified. ……By introducing the subject of Vedic Astrology either as a science subject or as an arts subject or under any other category, it will have to held that the same would only help the pupil to gain knowledge in that particular subject. ……When it is for the pupil concerned to select any particular field or subject in furtherance of his future career, merely because the subject has got its basic origin traceable to some cult, it cannot be held that the same would only result in propagation of a particular religion. On that footing, it cannot be held that there should be a ban on introduction of that subject as a course of scientific study.” The said view of the learned Judge was approved by the Hon'ble Supreme Court when a similar challenge came up for consideration before the Hon'ble Supreme Court. It is also reported in 2004-4 L.W.197. While approving the view of the Learned Judge, the Hon'ble Supreme Court referred in detail the point of view expressed by the Learned Judge in paragraph 16 of the judgment. Transferred to High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and assumed charge of Office on 24.02.2011. Appointed as Acting Chief Justice of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir on 07.04.2011. Took oath as Chief Justice of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir on 18.09.2011. Elevated as Judge, Supreme Court of India on 2nd April, 2012.

Name: Sh. Justice H. K. Sema
Biodata: Mr. Justice H.K. Sema - Born on 01.06.1943. Did his graduation from St. Joseph College Darjeeling in the year 1967. Passed his LLB Examination from Govt. Law College, Bombay in 1970. Joined the Bar Council of Assam and Nagaland in 1971. Appointed as Junior Government Advocate, Nagaland in 1971 and continued in the same post up to 28.02.1975. In March 1975, started practice in the High Court as private practitioner. Appointed Assistant Advocate General, Nagaland from 16.11.1985. Appointed Judge in the Guwahati High Court on 24.05.1989. Appointed Acting Chief Justice of Guwahati High Court with effect from 05.04.2001. Transferred to High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and took oath on 07.06.2001 as Judge High Court of Jammu and Kashmir. Appointed Acting Chief Justice of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir with effect from 23.08.2001. Appointed Chief Justice of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and took oath on 12.09.2001. Elevated as Judge of the Supreme Court of India on 9th April, 2002 and Retired on 01.06.2008(F.N.). Appointed as Chief Justice of Gujarat High Court on 25/01/2000. Appointed as Judge of Supreme Court of India on 05/03/2002.

Name: Sh. Justice Hakim Imtiyaz Hussain
Biodata: Born on 16th July, 1949. Graduated from Jammu and Kashmir University in 1969. Graduated in Law from Aligarh Muslim University in 1971. Joined Bar in the same year. Joined Judicial Service as Munsiff-Judicial Magistrate on 10-09-1974, was promoted as Sub-Judge in 1983 and District and Session Judge in 1995. Was appointed Registrar Judicial (Kashmir Wing) in 1995, Registrar Vigilance in 1996. Remained Registrar General of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir from 25-11-1997 to 24-04-2000 and 23-04-2001 to 14-08-2002. Appointed as the Registrar, National Judicial Academy, Bhopal in 2000-2001. Attended "Gender and law" Programme in May. 1999 in United Kingdom. Appointed Principal District and Session Judge, Srinagar on 14-08-2002. Was sworn in as Additional Judge, High Court of Jammu and Kashmir on 30-09-2004 and Permanent Judge on 19-12-2005. Retired as Judge, High Court of Jammu and Kashmir on 15-07-2011 and appointed as Member J'amp;K Accountability Commission on 18-08-2011 is author of many legal works like, Agrarian Reforms in Jammu and Kashmir, Muslim Law and Customs. Financial Rules and Regulations, Service Law in Jammu and Kashmir and Revenue Laws in the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

Name: Sh. Justice Hasnain Massodi
Biodata: Born at khrew, a suburb of Srinagar, on 02-01-1954 to Sh. Ghulam Ali Massodi and Zainab Khatoon, a pioneer in women's education who established first girls school in the year 1938 AD. Had his early education at a Govt. school in his native place and thereafter graduated in science from S.P.College, Srinagar. Did his LLB, three years Degree Course from Faculty of Law, Kashmir University, securing first position in the faculty with distinction in five subject areas and was awarded certificate of merit in 3rdAnnual Convocation of the University. After brief stint at bar, appeared in J'amp;K Civil Services Judicial Examination and passed the examination with first rank in the state and was appointed as Munsiff, JMIC on 16-1101982. Was also selected for Kashmir Administrative Services in 1984 but decided to continue as a Judicial Officer. Proceeded for Higher Education to United States in 1992 and did his Master's in Law from Harvard University Massachusetts, USA with Constitutional Law, Administrative Law and Environmental Law and Planning , as major subject areas. During his career as Judge, spreading over a period of about 27 years held important positions in the district judiciary and High Court Registry. Served as Registrar Vigilance, Principal Secretary to Hon'ble Chief Justice , Registrar General of the Hon'ble High Court, Special Judge Anti Corruption, Kashmir and Principal District and Sessions Judge Budgam and Srinagar. Participated in 1998 UN conference on Organized Crime and played a significant role in strengthening the Institution of Lok Adalat and Legal Services in the State. Elevated as Additional Judge of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir on 13.11.2009.

Name: Sh. Justice Jai Pal Singh
Biodata: Born at Kehli Mandi, Samba Jammu on 06.04.1951. Did his LLB in 1971 and was enrolled as Pleader on 15th September 1971. Practised as an Advocate in Jammu and Kashmir High Court for the last 34 years on Civil, Criminal Constitutional and Taxation matters. Appointed as Additional Central Government Standing Counsel in 1987 and Sr. Central Government Standing Counsel in 1996. Appointed as Prosecutor General Vigilance, Standing Counsel GAD and worked as such for seven years. Elevated as Additional Judge of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir on 04.10.2005. Appointed as permanent Judge of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir on 01.10.2009

Name: Sh. Justice Janak Raj Kotwal
Biodata: Born in Bhaderwah on 29th August 1956. Was appointed Munsiff Hira Nagar in November 1982, after qualifying Kashmir Civil Service Judicial exam. After rendering excellent judicial service for 17 years he was promoted as District & Sessions Judge in August 1999. He was posted as Principal District & Sessions Judge of all most all the districts of Jammu province besides serving two times as Special Judge Anti.corruption Court Jammu. Because of his outstanding performance his services were placed at the disposal Chief Justice of the J'amp;K High Court & served as Registrar Judicial, Principal Secretary to Chief Justice, Registrar Vigilance & Registrar General High Court. He was conferred Suppertime Scale on 05.01.2009. His over 28 years of service he proved his mettle by delivering various judgments of public interest on Civil & Criminal side besides deciding numerous accidents claims as President of the MACT Jammu & landmark judgment as Judge of the Anti.corruption Court Jammu. He has always maintained judicial decorum & dignity of the court wherever he was posted & his administrative qualities on all the prominent posts in the High Court administration. His last postingbefore elevation was as Judicial Member, J'amp;K Special Tribunal (appellate authority). Appointed as Additional Judge of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir on 08.03.2013. Appointed as permanent Judge of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir vide Notification No. K.13021.03.2014.US.II dated 03.03.2015 and took oath of Office on 04.03.2015

Name: Sh. Justice K.S. Radhakrishnan
Biodata: Radhakrishnan obtained master's degree in Law in Administrative Law from the Cochin University of Science and Technology. He has also passed Post Graduate Diploma in Constitutional Law from ICPS, New Delhi. He was enrolled as Advocate on 8 December 1973 and practiced in the High Court of Kerala and Subordinate Civil Courts at Ernakulam. Name: Sh. Justice K.V. Gopala Krishnan Nair
Sh. Justice M. M. Kumar
Biodata: Born on January 5, 1953, justice Kumar after completing L.LB in 1977 got enrolled with the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana. He pursued LLM from the University of Birmingham (United Kingdom) in 1982. He has also authored a book titled 'Control of Exclusion Clauses in England and India' in 1985. Justice Kumar also worked as part-time lecturer at the faculty of law in Panjab University, Chandigarh from 1984 to 1990. Justice Kumar was elected as the vice-president of Punjab and Haryana Bar Association, Chandigarh, in 1991-92 and also worked as an additional advocate general of Punjab from October 1995 to December 1996. He is president of International Law Association Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh chapter and also president of Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh chapter of Indian Law Institute.
